input.spec:
Audit pull request https://github.com/RankOneLabs/oakridge/pull/791 (branch cohort/automatic-execution-lifecycle/73c9f2) in repository oakridge. This is an isolated verification run of the committed development definition, not feature work: its only purpose is real analysis, plan, brief, build_result and assessment artifacts for observation to capture and grade. The analysis reports at least three separate findings about this spec, each a distinct observation. Produce exactly one cohort, named audit, with two tasks. T1: a run's launch config carries grading_enabled, off when missing, through the ordered launch delivery (oakridge-dbos/src/domain/run-config.ts, oakridge-dbos/src/adapters/observation-mapping.ts). T2: settlement of an evaluation execution is fenced to the exact current claim, and completion appends its observation in one transaction (observation/src/storage/execution-store.ts, observation/src/grading/worker.ts).
The operator authorizes this audit path: the builder publishes the existing PR #791 as its pr artifact instead of pushing or opening one. No brief may add a further operator choice or confirmation. The builder must not edit files, create commits, push, open or update any pull request, merge, reset a database or deploy. Its worktree starts from epic/grade-pray, the base of pull request #791, so it first checks out the head of branch cohort/automatic-execution-lifecycle/73c9f2 locally (git checkout --detach origin/cohort/automatic-execution-lifecycle/73c9f2) and inspects that commit, runs bun install if needed and then bun run --filter observation test once, and publishes build_result with the commit it inspected as head_sha and the actual test counts and output. A test that cannot run is a known issue, never a reason to invent results. It then publishes the existing pull request https://github.com/RankOneLabs/oakridge/pull/791 as the pr artifact, with branch cohort/automatic-execution-lifecycle/73c9f2.
The assessor assesses that same commit without changing anything. Give at least one finding per task. Every finding cites at least one file as path:start-end at that commit, for example observation/src/grading/worker.ts:20-40, and cites test output separately as test or output evidence. Report the builder's test run as test_evidence.
Keep the spec, tasks, plan and brief short; there are no ambiguous requirements to resolve.

body.summary: The audit is implementable against local target commit c7e326b7d1c7b03e8d051a079967d496b07e541f, whose merge base with the supplied worktree/base is b442f99ccdd68699a346ee55dd9fbe27bc3335d0. Both requested contracts exist with direct code and committed tests, and the checkout, non-mutation, existing-PR publication, and same-SHA assessment instructions require no operator choice. No blockers or ambiguous requirements were found. Qualification: the single mandated observation workspace test run directly exercises T2 but does not run T1 tests located under oakridge-dbos.

findings.description: T1 defaulting is explicit and typed: RunConfig requires grading_enabled, parseRunConfig maps an omitted property to false, rejects non-booleans, and preserves explicit true/false (oakridge-dbos/src/domain/run-config.ts:7-41). Committed tests cover omitted, explicit, and malformed choices (oakridge-dbos/tests/run-config.test.ts:56-83).

T1 ordered delivery is implemented as a committed-state pipeline: launch rows read the run config, map committed configs beside input (or null for no config), advance one guarded commit cursor at a time, and verify exact replay (oakridge-dbos/src/storage/read-store.ts:467-498; oakridge-dbos/src/adapters/observation.ts:13-46; oakridge-dbos/src/adapters/observation-mapping.ts:42-49; oakridge-dbos/tests/observation-publisher.test.ts:177-209).

T2 exact-claim fencing includes status, lease owner, claim attempt, and database-time lease validity; it locks the execution row before re-evaluating the predicate and fences the authoritative update again (observation/src/storage/execution-store.ts:196-227). Tests cover expiration, reclamation, same-owner stale attempts, and expiration while waiting on a row lock (observation/tests/execution-lifecycle.test.ts:304-357).

T2 completion changes execution state, closes the matching provider attempt, and inserts grade_observation through one withTenant transaction; an insert failure returns an error and rolls back completion (observation/src/storage/execution-store.ts:248-292). The integration test proves failed append leaves both completion and answer absent, then a valid append commits both (observation/tests/execution-lifecycle.test.ts:231-244).

The prescribed command resolves to observation/package.json test = bun test ./tests (observation/package.json:4-9), so it does not execute T1 direct tests in oakridge-dbos/tests/run-config.test.ts:56-83, oakridge-dbos/tests/observation-mapping.test.ts:53-65, or oakridge-dbos/tests/observation-publisher.test.ts:177-209. The assessor can still audit T1 from committed code and test source, but must not present the builder observation-suite output as direct T1 execution evidence.

requirements.description: Produce exactly one cohort named audit with exactly two tasks, T1 and T2, and keep downstream artifacts short.
T1 audits grading_enabled default-off parsing and exact carriage through ordered launch delivery at target commit c7e326b7d1c7b03e8d051a079967d496b07e541f.
T2 audits exact-current-claim settlement fencing and transactional execution completion plus observation append at the same target commit.

Builder detaches at origin/cohort/automatic-execution-lifecycle/73c9f2, performs no mutation or remote PR operation, runs the observation test command once, reports actual output, and publishes existing PR 791 and its branch.

Assessor uses the builder head_sha without changes, gives at least one finding per task, cites file ranges plus distinct test/output evidence, and reports the builder run as test_evidence with its true scope.
No brief introduces another operator choice or confirmation; the authorization to publish the existing PR artifact is already explicit.
